angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 550,299 km at 175.82 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6876 +/- 0.0178 mas (same row, RUWE 1.18): 175.82 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.791 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Yee et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-3693 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...70Y/abstract): 550,299 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.867 +/- 0.036 solar masses from Yee et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-3693 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...70Y/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5321 +/- 86 K from Yee et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3693 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...70Y/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Yee et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3693 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...70Y/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-3693.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.580, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
